summary: Gallatin County lookout built 1934 as a 60-foot steel tower and staffed by CCC crews; the tower is gone, but footings remain at a day-use picnic site.

facts.design: 60-foot steel stair tower with a dwelling, garage, latrine and picnic area (2025 FFLA report)
facts.status_note: Tower removed; the old tower's concrete footings remain on the site.

staffing.status: staffed by a Camp Cadiz Civilian Conservation Corps crew
staffing.as_of: the early days of the Shawnee National Forest

access.note: Forest Service day-use recreation site, open all year 6:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m.; overnight parking only outside the recreation site.

visit.trail_note: Picnic area with daytime parking and the trailhead for about five miles of trails below the knob. No restrooms and no potable water.

events.note: Constructed as a 60-foot steel stair tower with a dwelling, garage, latrine and picnic area (2025 FFLA report).

evidence.supports: Built in 1934 as a 60-foot steel stair tower with a dwelling, garage, latrine and picnic area
evidence.quote: The High Knob Tower was constructed in 1934 as a 60 feet steel stair tower. It included a dwelling, garage, latrine and a picnic area.

evidence.supports: Staffed by a Camp Cadiz CCC crew during the early days of the Shawnee National Forest
evidence.quote: Once the site of a fire lookout tower, high knob was staffed by the Camp Cadiz Civilian Conservation Corpsmen (CCC) during the early days of the Shawnee National Forest.
The old tower's concrete footings still remain.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Service page (last updated February 2025) places High Knob in the Hidden Springs Ranger District; the older Central Illinois list says Rosiclare Ranger District. The story does not name a district.

notes_for_editor: The 1934 build year rests on the 2025 FFLA chapter report, which describes a visit; no contemporary build record was read. height_m is converted from the 60-foot figure. No removal date is given; the 1972 bid notice is the latest dated fact. Staffing is from the Forest Service page and has no year. The FFLOS coordinates (37.60027, -88.32825) differ slightly from the Forest Service coordinates (37.60027778, -88.32805556). No new photos were found. The 'Southern Illinoisan' notice is quoted through the Central Illinois page.
